newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Soproni aims 23 pct market share in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Soproni aims 23 pct market share in 1997.

text.p: Hungarian brewery Soproni Sorgyar Rt wants to raise its market share to 23 percent this year, a company official said on Friday.

Together with Martfui, with which Soproni is merging, it had a combined market share of 21.3 percent in 1996, up from 19.2 percent in 1995, despite a continuous decline in beer consumption over the last years.

"We plan to increase our combined sales by 70,000-80,000 hectolitres this year from 1.56 million hectolitres in 1996," Arpad Nemeth, Soproni's deputy general director told Reuters on Friday following the company's annual general meeting.
Sorponi will pay a 15 percent dividend on ordinary shares and 16 percent on priority shares beginning with May 21.
The share exchange between Soproni for Martfui would happen within 90 days after the company court had registered the merger, he said.
Under the merger, Soproni will issue new shares for the exchange, raising its registered capital to 2.21 billion forints from 1.35 billion forints.
Both breweries are subsidiaries of Austrian brewery Brau Union AG.
Nemeth said the company would like to strengthen its 40 percent market share in the premium beers sector and targets a 65 percent share of the alcohol-free beers market.
He said the company will be unable to repeat last year's profit due to higher costs and extra taxes.
"Base material prices rose 40 percent over 1996, energy prices 35 percent and there is an additional 15 percent tax on beer," Nemeth said.

In 1996 Soproni posted a net profit of 830 million forints on net sales of 14.5 billion forints but this year they expect profit to be between 400 million and 500 million forints (not counting Martfui).
Nemeth said the company plans to improve distribution in Budapest and central and east Hungary.
The continuous decline in beer consumption over the last years would still plague the company.
"This trend is only likely to be reversed once real incomes start to grow," Nemeth said.
He added, however, that in the first quarter of 1997 sales grew one to two percent in volume terms and that this was an encouraging sign.

Before the merger, the products of the two breweries were marketed and sold by Brau Union Hungaria Kereskedelmi Kft, owned 60 percent by Soproni and 40 percent by Martfui. The trading company will now become the wholly-owned unit of Soproni, Nemeth said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Soproni shares closed at 5,850 forints, down 50.
